rows.verdict: Z2 has lower loss in every scenario for which a valid two-architecture comparison can be made; HV-S2 is not rankable because the Z1 operating point is physically inadmissible for the solid-solder model.

Z2 has lower peak temperature in HV-S1, where the gap exceeds twice the measured discretisation uncertainty. The approximately 1 C difference lies within the measured discretization uncertainty; therefore no thermal architecture ranking is drawn for HV-S0. HV-S2 is not rankable because the Z1 operating point is physically inadmissible for the solid-solder model.

Z1 has lower die warpage in every scenario for which a valid two-architecture comparison can be made; HV-S2 is not rankable because the Z1 operating point is physically inadmissible for the solid-solder model.

Z1 has lower joint displacement driver in every scenario for which a valid two-architecture comparison can be made; HV-S2 is not rankable because the Z1 operating point is physically inadmissible for the solid-solder model.

Z1 has lower local inelastic response in HV-S0, where the gap exceeds twice the measured discretisation uncertainty. In HV-S1 the difference lies within the measured discretisation uncertainty (and the Z1 response is extrapolated), so no ranking is drawn. HV-S2 is not rankable because the Z1 operating point is physically inadmissible for the solid-solder model.
